branding.nameLogoBody: Shown to learners in the app header and on emails.
branding.logoHint: PNG, SVG or JPEG, up to 512 KB. A square logo works best.
branding.logoError: Use a PNG, SVG or JPEG up to 512 KB.
branding.logoUnsafe: This SVG was refused: it contains a script, an event attribute or a reference outside the file (external image, font or link). Internal references (#id) are fine. Export it without them or upload a PNG.
branding.coloursBody: Primary is for actions and structure. Accent marks rewards: XP, streaks, the next step.
branding.senderHint: Emails go out as no-reply at this domain once it is verified.
branding.domainProofBody: Only a proven domain lets people with these addresses sign in with single sign-on and join automatically.
branding.proven: {domain} was proven on {date}. It is checked every day; if the record is missing for 7 days, the proof ends.
branding.notProven: Not proven yet. Add this TXT record to your DNS, then check.
branding.proofLapsing: The TXT record for {domain} has not been found since {since}. Unless it is restored, the proof ends on {date} and single sign-on and automatic joining for the domain stop. Add the record to your DNS again and select Check DNS.
branding.txtHint: Publish it on the domain itself or on the _cyclowareness subdomain.
branding.checkOk: Record found: the domain is proven.
branding.checkMissing: The record was not found. DNS changes can take up to an hour to spread.
branding.checkKept: The record was not found; the current proof stays in place. DNS changes can take up to an hour to spread.
branding.checkInvalid: Enter a domain such as agency.gov.az.
branding.domainTaken: Another organisation has already verified this domain.
branding.sampleSubtitle: Four signs that give a fake email away.

languages.yourBody: Only for you: the console, the learner app and your notifications. The organisation's settings below stay as they are.
languages.defaultBody: New learners start in this language. Each person can switch later.
languages.availableBody: Learners can pick only from these.
languages.timeZoneBody: The organisation's clock: due dates end at 23:59 in this zone, streak days and daily XP turn over at its midnight, scheduled reports go out at 08:00, and every date and time is shown in it.

identity.ssoBody: Staff sign in with their organisation account: Entra ID, ADFS, Keycloak, Okta or Google.
identity.adminNote: Administrators always sign in with their own password and two-step code, never through single sign-on.
identity.step1Body: Your identity provider must support OpenID Connect.
identity.oidcHint: Works with Entra ID, Keycloak, Okta and Google.
identity.step2Title: Add Cyclowareness to your identity provider
identity.step2Body: Create a web app there and register this redirect URI.
identity.checkFailed: Enter an https issuer URL and a client ID.
identity.testSignInHint: Uses the saved settings, so save first. You come back here with the result.
identity.testOk: Test sign-in worked: the provider confirmed the account and sent an email address.
identity.testFailed: Test sign-in failed. Check the issuer URL, client ID, secret, redirect URI and email claim. The audit log shows the reason.
identity.samlNotConnected: Sign-in through SAML is not connected yet. Use OpenID Connect.
identity.secretHint: Stored encrypted. It is never shown again.
identity.secretSet: A secret is saved. Type a new one to replace it.
identity.secretReenter: The server has changed. Enter the secret again: the saved one is never sent to a different server.
identity.confirmHint: Whoever controls the identity provider can sign in as this organisation's people. Confirm the change with your own password; it is recorded.
identity.ldapBody: People removed from the directory are suspended, not deleted.
identity.connectorNote: The settings are stored now. The directory connector runs in the on-premises worker, which needs network access to your domain controller.
identity.caCertificateHint: PEM text of the authority that signed the server certificate. Needed for ldaps with a private CA.
identity.certificatePinHint: Hex fingerprint of the server certificate. The connector refuses any other certificate.
identity.samlEntryPointHint: The SingleSignOnService URL from the provider's metadata.
identity.samlCertificateHint: PEM text from the provider's metadata.
identity.samlNote: The SAML details are stored now. The SAML exchange itself is not connected yet: sign-in runs through OpenID Connect.
identity.require2faBody: Everyone with console access (admins, analysts, campaign managers, content creators, department heads and executives) must turn on two-step verification before they can open the console.
identity.maxDevices: Maximum devices signed in at once

email.deliveryBody: Invite and password links go out through your own mail server.
email.sendLinksBody: Active only after a successful test email.
email.simulationBody: Phishing simulations go out from this look-alike address; every other message keeps the sender above. The address's domain is proven first with the same TXT record as in Branding → Domain proof, and your mail server must be allowed to send for it (SPF, DKIM).
email.simulationFromHint: Optional. Prove the domain with Check DNS before saving.
email.simulationProven: {domain} is proven: addresses on it can be saved.
email.simulationNotProven: No look-alike domain is proven yet. Enter the address, publish the TXT record on its domain, then check.
email.testBody: Sends a real message through the saved settings.
email.passwordReenter: The server or port has changed. Enter the password again: the saved one is never sent to a different server.
email.passwordSet: A password is saved. Type a new one to replace it.
email.testText: This is a test email from the security awareness portal. If you can read it, the mail server settings work.
email.testOk: Test email sent. Sending is now active.

testErrors.invalid_address: the recipient address is not valid
testErrors.not_configured: the server or the sender address is incomplete
testErrors.blocked_destination: only mail servers on the public internet (ports 25, 465, 587, 2525) are accepted
testErrors.connection_failed: the server could not be reached
testErrors.auth_failed: the user name or password was not accepted
testErrors.tls_error: the TLS connection could not be established
testErrors.send_failed: the server did not accept the message
testErrors.unresolvable: the mail server's name could not be resolved (DNS)

email.outboxBody: The last 20 messages. Without a mail server they are kept here as “logged”.
email.resendAll: {count, plural, one {Resend the failed message} other {Resend # failed messages}}
email.resent: {count, plural, =0 {There is nothing to resend.} one {# message is back in the queue.} other {# messages are back in the queue.}}
email.resendFailed: The messages could not be queued again.
email.campaignCancelled: Not sent: the campaign was cancelled

notifications.banner: Nothing is emailed until email is set up and a test mail succeeds.
notifications.bannerReadyBody: Emails go out through your mail server.
notifications.templatesBody: One template per message and language.
notifications.subject: Subject
notifications.templateEmpty: The “{kind}” template ({language}) needs a subject and a message.
notifications.templateNoLink: The message of the “{kind}” template ({language}) must contain {token}: it is the link people use to open the training.
notifications.managerAlertsBody: Tell managers when someone in their team needs attention.

attestation.title: Confirmation text
attestation.body: Learners confirm this after the last lesson of a module. Only then does the module count as completed.

certificate.textBody: Learners get this certificate for every module they finish. An empty field uses the default text.
certificate.title: Title
certificate.titleHint: Leave empty to use the default title.
certificate.publicLinkBody: Anyone with the link sees the name, module and date.

learning.timeLimitsCardBody: Applies to every learner of your organisation.
learning.timeLimitsBody: Some questions in medium and hard modules run on a timer. When time is up, the question counts as a wrong answer.
learning.refresherBody: While a learner's risk score is at or above the threshold, once a month they are asked to finish their next open training module within 14 days. No XP is lost.
learning.thresholdHint: A higher number means fewer refreshers. Default 67.
learning.dailyGoalBody: XP a learner aims for each day.

protection.contentBody: Keeps lessons and staff data from being copied.
protection.copyingBody: Text cannot be selected or copied, printing gives a blank page and the screen blurs when the window is left.
protection.watermarkBody: Marks every screen with a code only the leak check can read.
protection.android: Screenshot and screen recording block in the Android app
protection.androidBody: Casting or mirroring to a projector turns black too. Needs app version 1.1.3 or later.
protection.leakBody: Every screen carries a code people cannot see. The code tells whose screen a picture came from.
protection.step1: Find the code in the picture
protection.dropHint: Choose or paste a picture. It is processed in this browser only.
protection.enhanced: Contrast boosted: look for the repeated code (XXXX-XXXX).
protection.retentionBody: The daily clean-up deletes this organisation's older records. Lesson progress, XP, confirmations and certificates are always kept.
protection.auditMonthsHint: 0, or 12 to 120. 0 keeps everything; the audit log is kept at least a year.

integrations.webhookBody: Sends events as signed JSON to your SIEM or ticket system.
integrations.addressHint: Starts with https://. Public address, port 443.
integrations.secretBody: Your receiver uses it to check that a request came from us.
integrations.secretShown: Copy it now, it won't be shown again:
integrations.testNoTarget: Save a webhook address or a syslog server first.
integrations.syslogBody: Forward events to your SIEM over syslog.
integrations.portHint: Allowed ports: {ports}. Usually 6514 for TLS and 514 for TCP and UDP.
integrations.hdrSignature: Every request is signed: sha256= plus the HMAC of the body, made with your secret.
integrations.hdrTimestamped: Signature that also covers the timestamp: sha256= plus the HMAC of the timestamp, a dot and the body.
integrations.hdrTimestamp: Unix time of this attempt, in seconds.
integrations.hdrDelivery: Unique per event and the same on retries: use it to skip repeats.
integrations.receiverVerify: Verify the timestamped signature and reject requests whose timestamp is more than 5 minutes from your clock.
integrations.recipeBody: ServiceNow: create a Scripted REST API, verify the signature in its script and open an incident for each event. Jira: put a small relay in front of an Automation incoming webhook that verifies the signature, then let the rule create an issue.
integrations.apiTokensBody: Read-only access for other systems: an HR or BI tool downloads reports and the people list with a token instead of a sign-in. Up to {max} active tokens.
integrations.tokenShown: Copy the token now; it won't be shown again.
integrations.tokenNameHint: What uses it, for example the HR system.
integrations.tokenLimit: The limit of {max} active tokens is reached. Revoke one first.
integrations.tokenPlan: Your organisation's plan doesn't include integrations, so new tokens can't be created. You can still revoke existing ones.

security.title: Support access
security.body: Safarov Industries support can create a one-time sign-in link for an administrator of your organisation only while you allow it. Every link is recorded in your audit log and the administrator is told by email.
security.grant: Allow Safarov Industries support access for 72 hours
